conventions.convention: Posterior prediction takes a supplied probability kernel with probability sections at every data value. The dominated construction requires a proper prior, a sigma-finite data measure and a specified jointly measurable sampling density; its null-fiber filling belongs to the selected version.
Credible sets have product-measurable membership graphs and posterior mass at least 1−α at every point of their declared data domain; the definition permits α∈[0,1].
For fixed u∈(0,1), the lower quantile is the real infimum of canonical rational r satisfying Π_y((−∞,r])≥u. Its bracket uses an open lower tail and a closed upper tail.
A median has at least half the posterior mass on each closed side; it need not be unique.

Loss is nonnegative and jointly measurable. Posterior risk is defined only for finite loss integrals. A Bayes action rule is measurable on a declared measurable data domain and attains the minimum among finite-risk actions at every point of that domain.
The squared-loss mean rule is asserted on the measurable finite-second-moment domain and explicitly assumes AC through the L²-projection supplier.

Predictive moment identities require a finite mixture second moment and zero-fill future means and variances outside the finite-second-moment parameter set. Their kernel formulation is choice-free; AC is used only for the optional conditional-expectation-class interpretation.
Finite-class zero–one classification uses a nonempty finite class with its full sigma-algebra and selects the least index among posterior-mass maximizers.

load_bearing.statement: For a probability kernel Π_y on R and u∈(0,1), q_u(y)=inf{r∈Q:F_y(r)≥u} exists as a real number, is measurable, and satisfies Π_y((−∞,q_u(y)))≤u≤Π_y((−∞,q_u(y)]).

A pointwise Bayes action at y is a finite-risk action attaining the minimum among all finite-risk actions. On a declared measurable data domain D, a Bayes action rule is a measurable map δ:D→A whose finite posterior risk attains that minimum at every y∈D.

For probability kernels Π:Y→Θ and Q:Θ→Z, the mixture Q_y^pred(B)=∫Q_θ(B)Π_y(dθ) is a probability kernel and integrates every nonnegative measurable future function by the displayed iterated-integral formula.
For a posterior probability kernel on R and 0<α<1, C_α(y)=[q_{α/2}(y),q_{1−α/2}(y)] is graph-measurable and Π_y(C_α(y))≥1−α for every y.
A posterior credible set at level 1−α is a graph-measurable set-valued rule C with Π_y(C(y))≥1−α for every y in its declared data domain.
Let Π be a posterior probability kernel on R. The rule m(y)=q_{1/2}(y) is measurable and is a posterior median on every data fiber.
If ∫s₂(θ)Π_y(dθ)<∞, the predictive mean is ∫μ dΠ_y and the predictive variance is ∫v dΠ_y+Var_{Π_y}(μ), with the stated zero-filled moment convention.
On the measurable domain D₁={y:∫|θ|Π_y(dθ)<∞}, every posterior median minimizes finite absolute posterior risk, and the measurable lower-median rule is an attained Bayes action rule.

On a nonempty finite class with all subsets measurable and zero–one loss, every posterior-mass maximizer minimizes pointwise posterior risk; the least-indexed maximizer is a measurable finite-risk Bayes action rule, without choice.

concerns.concern: Facts & Assumptions F2 writes the bracket with literal '(-infty,q_u(y))' and '(-infty,q_u(y)]' instead of '(-\infty,q_u(y))' and '(-\infty,q_u(y)]'. The Statement and proof use the intended infinity notation correctly; this is a notation/rendering defect in F2.

seams_checked.note: The prerequisite page and its fiberwise normalization items distinguish finite-positive-evidence updates from globally supplied posterior kernels. The consumer retains the proper-prior, probability-sampling-kernel, sigma-finite data measure and jointly measurable density hypotheses for the published dominated formula, and retains null-fiber version dependence.

Checked the quantile-stabilization lemma, linear and nonlinear functional coverage theorems, and CDF/multiscale credible-band theorem. Their citations preserve the rational lower-quantile convention, measurability and CDF bracket, and posterior mass at least 1−α. Frequentist calibration is obtained from additional BvM, sampling-center and continuous-limit-quantile hypotheses rather than attributed to credibility alone.
